requirements.evidence: All contract pieces are present: migrations (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_queues_table.php, ...000002_create_tickets_table.php:26-27 unique (queue_id, code) + recommended index), Queue/Ticket models with casts and relations (app/Models/Ticket.php:23-32,57-65), Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:130-133), enums, InactiveQueueException, invokable IssueTicket matching the signature (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:16-20), factories. Inactive queue is re-read with lockForUpdate inside the transaction (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:33-37) and nextCode handles A999->A1000 and malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:73-90). Gaps are edge cases: write-once only via model events (app/Models/Ticket.php:46-54) so query-builder updates bypass it; call() has no lock/refresh (app/Models/Ticket.php:99-119); nextCode reuses a number when the highest ticket is deleted.

conventions.evidence: Follows the main conventions: domain write is an action class (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php), migrations are Laravel-generated style with reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000002_create_tickets_table.php:34-37), deliberate fillable via #[Fillable] (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:14), factories exist, and both docs required by the task were updated (docs/business-rules.md '### Queue'/'**Single call**', docs/database-schema.md). Deviations: authorization is a direct EntityMembership query instead of a policy/gate (app/Models/Ticket.php:103-109), CHANGELOG.md is not updated under [Unreleased], and the change ships no tests despite the mandatory TDD rule.

security.evidence: Server-side authorization is enforced in Ticket::call() with an EntityMembership exists() check before any write (app/Models/Ticket.php:103-109); priority is validated server-side (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:21-23); mass assignment is constrained deliberately (app/Models/Ticket.php:14) and the queue state is re-read under lock rather than trusted from the passed model (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:33-37). No unescaped output, secrets or client-trusted IDs, but authorization bypasses the project's policy/gate layer and call() does not lock the row, leaving a double-call race.

tests.evidence: The whole diff (589 lines) contains only app/, database/ and docs/ files; there is no tests/ file and no 'summarized' note, so no Pest/PHPUnit test covers the action, nextCode, write-once, call(), authorization rejection, inactive queue or factories.

simplicity.evidence: Lean and direct overall: one action, model methods, two small enums, generated migrations and factories; no service/repository layers. Minor redundancy: code allocation exists both as a model creating hook (app/Models/Ticket.php:39-43) and explicitly in the action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:41), and the InactiveQueueException catch only rethrows (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:48-49).

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods with useful docblocks (app/Models/Ticket.php:67-90, 92-98; app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:30-32). Small blemishes: redundant duplicate type check in isUniqueViolation (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:62-63) and a nested while(true)/try/catch with a bare continue (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-57) that takes a moment to follow; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the action, enums, exception, models, factories, two migrations and exactly the two docs the task told the agent to update (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md); no unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (no call-next selection, UI, totem API or cancellation).

issues.explanation: The change ships zero tests, while the project requires test-first coverage for everything implemented, including the inactive-queue rejection, code allocation, write-once, single-call and authorization paths.

Write-once is enforced only through the model's updating event, so an Eloquent query-builder update such as Ticket::where(...)->update(['priority' => 5]) changes a protected field without throwing LogicException, which the task's 'any Eloquent save/update' wording requires.

call() checks the in-memory status and saves without locking or refreshing the row, so two concurrent callers can both pass the waiting check and the ticket is effectively called twice, weakening the 'exactly once' invariant.

nextCode uses 'last valid code + 1', so deleting the highest-numbered ticket reuses its number (A001..A003, delete A003, next is A003), contradicting the stated rule that deleting a ticket does not reuse its number; the task text is itself ambiguous here, so this is worth confirming rather than asserting a bug.
Authorization for calling a ticket is a hand-written EntityMembership exists() query rather than a policy/gate, contrary to the convention that authorization always goes through app/Policies.
The conventions require keeping docs in sync, including a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased], but no changelog entry accompanies the new queue/ticket domain.

The dedicated InactiveQueueException catch exists only to rethrow the same exception so it is not caught by the QueryException handler; catching QueryException alone would achieve the same behaviour with less code.
isUniqueViolation checks the same value twice, `$e->getCode() === '23000' || (string) $e->getCode() === '23000'`, which is redundant.

review.summary: The change implements the queue/ticket persistence and domain core (models, enums, exception, IssueTicket action, factories and the two required docs) largely faithfully to the contract, including the locked inactive-queue re-read and the display-code rules. It is not mergeable yet because it ships no tests at all, and it has smaller gaps around write-once enforcement, concurrent double calls and policy-based authorization.
